name: Photography
description: How a still photograph was made: light, exposure, focus, lens, composition, process and faults. Words the booru sets lack.

entries.name: portrait
entries.description: A picture made to show a particular person, with the face or figure dominating the frame. The sitter usually knows about the camera. Use [candid](#candid) when they did not, and [group_portrait](#group_portrait) when more than one person is the subject.

entries.name: selfie
entries.description: Made at arm's length or on a stick with the camera held by the subject, usually a phone's front lens. The near arm, the low or high angle and the wide field give it away. Use [self_portrait](#self_portrait) for a composed sitting.

entries.name: candid
entries.description: Someone photographed without posing, often without noticing. Expression and gesture are unarranged and the framing is whatever the moment allowed. Use [street_portrait](#street_portrait) when the person was approached and knew about the picture.

entries.name: group_portrait
entries.description: Several people arranged and photographed together, all of them aware of the camera. Use [family_portrait](#family_portrait), [team_photo](#team_photo) or [school_portrait](#school_portrait) for the named occasions, and [crowd_shot](#crowd_shot) when nobody was arranged.

entries.name: headshot
entries.description: A tight [portrait](#portrait) of head and shoulders made for a purpose: casting, a staff page, a profile picture. Plain background, even light, sharp eyes, no distractions. Use portrait for a close portrait made for its own sake.

entries.name: posed_portrait
entries.description: The sitter has been arranged: told where to stand, how to turn, what to do with the hands. Tag it when the direction is visible in the result. Contrast [candid](#candid), where nothing was asked for.

entries.name: self_portrait
entries.description: The photographer as subject, deliberately: tripod, timer or remote release, composed like any other sitting. Use [selfie](#selfie) for the arm's-length phone picture and [mirror_selfie](#mirror_selfie) when a mirror does the work.

entries.name: studio_portrait
entries.description: Made against a seamless, painted or draped background under controlled light, with nothing of a real place visible. The backdrop may be plain or patterned but it is clearly a backdrop. Contrast [environmental_portrait](#environmental_portrait).

entries.name: beauty_photography
entries.description: Tight on the face for skin, make-up, hair or nails, lit flatteringly and [retouched](#retouched) closely. The product is the look, not the clothes. Use [headshot](#headshot) when the picture is an identity record instead.

entries.name: child_portrait
entries.description: A single child as the subject, at play or sitting for the camera. Use [newborn_photography](#newborn_photography) for the first weeks and [school_portrait](#school_portrait) for the annual classroom sitting.

entries.name: corporate_portrait
entries.description: A person photographed for their employer: staff page, annual report, press kit. Usually a suit, a lobby or an office wall, and a friendly but neutral expression. Use [headshot](#headshot) when it is [cropped](#cropped) to head and shoulders on a plain ground.

entries.name: couple_portrait
entries.description: Two people photographed as a pair, usually touching or turned towards each other. Use [engagement_session](#engagement_session) for the pictures made before a wedding and [family_portrait](#family_portrait) once children are in the frame.

entries.name: crowd_shot
entries.description: Many people in the frame with no one of them the subject: an audience, a market, a platform, a march. Nobody was arranged and faces may be small or turned away. Use [group_portrait](#group_portrait) when the people posed.

entries.name: environmental_portrait
entries.description: The sitter photographed in the place that explains them, with the surroundings given as much room as the person. The room is part of the picture, not a background. Contrast [studio_portrait](#studio_portrait); use [occupational_portrait](#occupational_portrait) when the place is specifically their work.

entries.name: event_photography
entries.description: Coverage of a gathering as it happens: a party, conference, launch or ceremony, with speakers, guests and handshakes. Use the named kinds where they fit, such as [wedding_photography](#wedding_photography) or [concert_photography](#concert_photography).

entries.name: family_portrait
entries.description: A household photographed together, on a sofa, in a park or in a studio, dressed for the occasion. Use [couple_portrait](#couple_portrait) for two adults alone and [child_portrait](#child_portrait) when one child is the subject.

entries.name: fashion_editorial
entries.description: A styled fashion story with a mood or narrative rather than a plain record of the garment: locations, props, dramatic poses. Use [lookbook](#lookbook) for the straight commercial version of the same clothes.

entries.name: fashion_photography
entries.description: A picture made to show clothes or accessories on a person, with styling, hair and make-up arranged for the garment. Use [beauty_photography](#beauty_photography) when the face rather than the outfit is the product.

entries.name: full_length_portrait
entries.description: The whole figure from head to feet inside the frame, standing, sitting or leaning. Use [headshot](#headshot) for head and shoulders, and [group_portrait](#group_portrait) when several people are shown this way.

entries.name: mirror_selfie
entries.description: The subject photographs their [reflection](#reflection), so the phone or camera is visible in the frame, often with a bathroom or fitting room around it. Tag [street_style](#street_style) instead when the point is the outfit rather than the mirror.

entries.name: street_portrait
entries.description: A stranger approached in public and photographed on the spot, usually with their assent: they face the camera and the street stays around them. Contrast [candid](#candid), where nobody was asked, and [environmental_portrait](#environmental_portrait), which is arranged in advance.

entries.name: wedding_photography
entries.description: Coverage of a wedding day, from preparations through ceremony to reception, mixing posed groups with [candid](#candid) moments. Use [bridal_portrait](#bridal_portrait) for a single formal sitting and [engagement_session](#engagement_session) for the pictures made beforehand.

entries.name: boudoir
entries.description: An intimate private sitting in lingerie or bedding, made in a bedroom or hotel room and intended for the sitter themselves. Use [glamour_photography](#glamour_photography) for the more public styled version and [nude](#nude) when nothing is worn.

entries.name: bridal_portrait
entries.description: A formal single [portrait](#portrait) of the person in the wedding dress or suit, often made away from the day itself. Use [wedding_photography](#wedding_photography) for coverage of the event and [couple_portrait](#couple_portrait) when both partners are in the frame.

entries.name: concert_photography
entries.description: Performers on a lit stage, shot from the pit or the floor, with coloured stage light and dark surroundings. Use [dance_photography](#dance_photography) for staged movement work and [crowd_shot](#crowd_shot) when the audience is the subject.

entries.name: cosplay_photography
entries.description: Someone photographed in a costume they made or bought, posed in character, at a convention or on location. The costume and the pose are the point. Use [fashion_photography](#fashion_photography) when clothes are shown as clothes.

entries.name: dance_photography
entries.description: Dancers photographed for the line of the body: a held pose, a jump caught at its top, or a blurred sweep of movement. Use [concert_photography](#concert_photography) for performance coverage in stage light.

entries.name: documentary_portrait
entries.description: A [portrait](#portrait) made as part of a reportage or long-term project: the person stops for the camera but nothing is styled or lit for effect. Use [candid](#candid) when they never stopped and [editorial_portrait](#editorial_portrait) when it was staged for a story.

entries.name: editorial_portrait
entries.description: A [portrait](#portrait) made to accompany an article: a subject given a setting, a prop or a strong lighting idea that says something about the story. Use [corporate_portrait](#corporate_portrait) for the plain company sitting.

entries.name: engagement_session
entries.description: A relaxed outdoor or at-home sitting for a couple before their wedding, walking, laughing, holding hands. Use [couple_portrait](#couple_portrait) when there is no wedding attached and [wedding_photography](#wedding_photography) for the day itself.

entries.name: figure_study
entries.description: A formal study of the body as shape, line and light, often anonymous with the face turned away or [cropped](#cropped) out. Use [nude](#nude) for the broader case and [portrait](#portrait) when the picture is about who the person is.

entries.name: glamour_photography
entries.description: A flattering, sensual [portrait](#portrait) made to present the person attractively, with styled hair, make-up and clothing. Softer and more public than [boudoir](#boudoir); use [pin_up](#pin_up) for the deliberately retro version.

entries.name: graduation_portrait
entries.description: The end-of-school or end-of-degree sitting: gown, cap, diploma, sometimes a campus background. Includes the final-year portraits made months before the ceremony. Use [school_portrait](#school_portrait) for the ordinary annual sitting.

entries.name: group_selfie
entries.description: Several people crowded into a phone held by one of them, heads leaning together towards the lens. Use [group_portrait](#group_portrait) when someone else took the picture from a distance.

entries.name: lookbook
entries.description: Plain commercial pictures of a collection: one outfit per frame, repeated pose, clean background, the garment readable from every angle. Use [fashion_editorial](#fashion_editorial) when the picture tells a story instead.

entries.name: maternity_portrait
entries.description: A pregnant person photographed for the pregnancy, the [silhouette](#silhouette) of the belly given deliberately. Often outdoors at dusk or in a studio with draped fabric. Use [family_portrait](#family_portrait) when it becomes a picture of everyone.

entries.name: newborn_photography
entries.description: A baby in its first weeks, usually asleep, wrapped or curled on blankets, in soft even light. Use [child_portrait](#child_portrait) once the child sits up and looks back at the camera.

entries.name: nude
entries.description: The unclothed human body as the subject of the picture. Use [figure_study](#figure_study) for the formal study of shape and light, [implied_nude](#implied_nude) when nothing is actually shown, and [boudoir](#boudoir) when clothing remains.

entries.name: occupational_portrait
entries.description: A person shown at their trade, with the tools, uniform or workplace that name the job. A narrower kind of [environmental_portrait](#environmental_portrait); use that one when the setting characterises the sitter without being their work.

entries.name: passport_photo
entries.description: Made to a document standard: plain light background, head square to the camera, neutral expression, no shadow and no glasses glare. Use [headshot](#headshot) for a professional [portrait](#portrait) that merely looks plain.

entries.name: photobooth
entries.description: Made in a coin-operated booth: a strip or grid of small frames, hard frontal [flash](#flash), a curtain behind. Faces are close and expressions change from frame to frame. Not the same as a plain [passport_photo](#passport_photo).

entries.name: pin_up
entries.description: A playful, retro-styled picture in the manner of mid-century poster art: exaggerated pose, bright colour, period hair and clothing. Use [glamour_photography](#glamour_photography) for the modern equivalent without the period styling.

entries.name: profile_portrait
entries.description: The sitter turned a full quarter turn so the face reads as an outline against the background. Only one eye and one ear are visible. A three-quarter turn is an ordinary [portrait](#portrait), not this.

entries.name: promotional_portrait
entries.description: A publicity picture of a performer, band, author or speaker made to be handed out with a release or listing. Confident pose, clean styling, room for a caption. Use [editorial_portrait](#editorial_portrait) when it illustrates an article.

entries.name: red_carpet
entries.description: Arrivals photographed against a sponsor backdrop with direct [flash](#flash): a step, a turn, a pause to be seen. Use [promotional_portrait](#promotional_portrait) for a made picture and [event_photography](#event_photography) for the rest of the evening.

entries.name: runway_photography
entries.description: Models walking a catwalk, shot head-on from the end of the runway with hard show lighting and a dark surround. Use [fashion_editorial](#fashion_editorial) for a staged shoot and [event_photography](#event_photography) for the room around the show.

entries.name: school_portrait
entries.description: The annual school sitting: a mottled or graduated backdrop, one child at a time, or the whole class in rows. Recognisable by the uniform look of the lighting and pose. Use [graduation_portrait](#graduation_portrait) for the leaving year.

entries.name: street_style
entries.description: A person photographed on the pavement for what they are wearing, walking or stopped for a moment, city behind them. Use [street_portrait](#street_portrait) when the picture is about the person and [fashion_editorial](#fashion_editorial) for a styled shoot.

entries.name: team_photo
entries.description: A sports side, band or crew lined up in rows, kit on, often with a trophy or ball in front. The arrangement is formulaic and everyone faces the camera. Use [group_portrait](#group_portrait) for an unlabelled group.

entries.name: implied_nude
entries.description: The subject reads as unclothed but nothing is shown: sheets, shadow, an arm or the frame edge cover what would be. Use [nude](#nude) when the body is actually visible.

entries.name: mugshot
entries.description: The booking photograph: frontal and profile frames against a height chart or a bare wall, flat [flash](#flash), often a card with a number. Its look is imitated in styled sittings, which still take this tag.

entries.name: paparazzi_shot
entries.description: A well-known person photographed unaware and unwilling, usually from a distance with a long lens or through glass. Awkward framing and motion are typical. Use [candid](#candid) for the ordinary unposed picture.

entries.name: landscape
entries.description: A wide view of natural or worked country where the place itself is the subject. Use it for the whole scene; for a close view of one patch within it use [intimate_landscape](#intimate_landscape), and for water-dominated views [seascape](#seascape).

entries.name: architecture_photography
entries.description: A building or structure photographed for its form, materials and geometry, normally with verticals kept straight. Inside spaces are [interior_photography](#interior_photography); a whole quarter of a city is [cityscape](#cityscape).

entries.name: cityscape
entries.description: A city seen whole or in a large slice: rooftops, blocks, river frontage, streets from above. A single building belongs in [architecture_photography](#architecture_photography).

entries.name: macro_photography
entries.description: Small subjects photographed at or near life size, so detail invisible to the eye fills the frame. Past a few times magnification, through a microscope, use [photomicrography](#photomicrography).

entries.name: nature_photography
entries.description: The natural world as subject — plants, animals, terrain, weather — with no built or human focus. A broad umbrella; prefer [wildlife_photography](#wildlife_photography), [botanical_photography](#botanical_photography) or [landscape](#landscape) when one of them fits.

entries.name: travel_photography
entries.description: Pictures made away from home that describe a place: its streets, markets, transport, weather and look. Broader than [landscape](#landscape) or [cityscape](#cityscape), and usually mixing them.

entries.name: wildlife_photography
entries.description: Wild animals in their own habitat, usually at a distance with a long lens. Captive animals belong in [zoo_photography](#zoo_photography), and a remotely triggered picture in [camera_trap](#camera_trap).

entries.name: aerial_photography
entries.description: Taken from the air — aircraft, helicopter, balloon or drone — looking down or obliquely at the ground. A view from a tall building or a hilltop is still [cityscape](#cityscape) or [landscape](#landscape).

entries.name: astrophotography
entries.description: The night sky as the subject: stars, planets, nebulae, the band of the galaxy. Once land or a building shares the frame the picture is a [nightscape](#nightscape).

entries.name: bird_photography
entries.description: Birds as the subject, perched, feeding or displaying, typically long lens and fast shutter. For airborne shots use [birds_in_flight](#birds_in_flight).

entries.name: coastal_photography
entries.description: Where land meets sea — cliffs, beaches, headlands, harbours, tide pools. Use [seascape](#seascape) when the water and horizon dominate and the land is incidental.

entries.name: drone_photography
entries.description: Shot from a small remotely piloted aircraft: low heights, clean geometry, viewpoints no crewed aircraft could hold. A subset of [aerial_photography](#aerial_photography).

entries.name: interior_photography
entries.description: The inside of a building as designed space — rooms, halls, stairwells, lobbies — usually with corrected verticals and window light balanced against the lamps. A shoot made to sell the property is [real_estate_photography](#real_estate_photography).

entries.name: mountain_photography
entries.description: High country photographed from below or from among it: peaks, ridges, glaciers, alpine valleys. A range seen from an aircraft is [aerial_photography](#aerial_photography) instead.

entries.name: nightscape
entries.description: A [landscape](#landscape) or [cityscape](#cityscape) under a starry sky, the ground lit by moon, late [twilight](#twilight) or light painting. Distinct from [astrophotography](#astrophotography), where the sky alone matters.

entries.name: seascape
entries.description: The sea as the main subject: open water, surf, horizon, usually with a lot of sky. If cliffs, beach or harbour carry the picture instead, use [coastal_photography](#coastal_photography).

entries.name: skyline
entries.description: The city's profile against the sky, usually from a distance or across water. A subset of [cityscape](#cityscape) in which the [silhouette](#silhouette) itself is the picture.

entries.name: underwater_photography
entries.description: Made with the camera below the surface in a housing, with the colour loss, backscatter and [strobe](#strobe) lighting that follow. A picture of the sea from above is [seascape](#seascape).

entries.name: woodland_photography
entries.description: Inside a forest rather than looking at one — trunks, understorey, filtered light, no horizon. The tangle and the absence of an obvious subject are what make it its own discipline.

entries.name: abstract_nature
entries.description: Natural material — [ice](#ice), bark, sand, water, lichen — framed until it reads as [pattern](#pattern) and colour rather than as a thing or a place. Related to [intimate_landscape](#intimate_landscape), but with no sense of scale left.

entries.name: adventure_photography
entries.description: Movement through wild country — climbing, paddling, skiing, riding — with the terrain as much the subject as the action. Where nothing is being done, [landscape](#landscape) or [mountain_photography](#mountain_photography) fits better.

entries.name: architectural_abstract
entries.description: Built surfaces [cropped](#cropped) until the building is unrecognisable: repeating panels, curves, shadow bands. If a viewer can still tell what structure it is, [architectural_detail](#architectural_detail) fits better.

entries.name: architectural_detail
entries.description: One part of a building filling the frame — a cornice, a stair, a window bay, a joint. Still readable as a piece of architecture, unlike [architectural_abstract](#architectural_abstract).

entries.name: aurora_photography
entries.description: Northern or southern lights over a [landscape](#landscape), usually exposures of a few seconds at high sensitivity. Use [nightscape](#nightscape) for a starry sky with no auroral curtains in it.

entries.name: birds_in_flight
entries.description: A bird photographed airborne, wings out, tracked and panned against sky or water. The demanding subset of [bird_photography](#bird_photography), with its own look and its own failures.

entries.name: botanical_photography
entries.description: Plants and flowers as the subject, in the field or on a plain ground, with the structure of the specimen clear. A planted, designed space is [garden_photography](#garden_photography).

entries.name: conservation_photography
entries.description: Nature photographed to make a case: habitat loss, pollution, restoration, species under pressure. Overlaps [nature_photography](#nature_photography) and [wildlife_photography](#wildlife_photography), but is framed as an argument rather than a [portrait](#portrait) of a place.

entries.name: deep_sky
entries.description: Faint nebulae, galaxies and clusters built from many tracked exposures stacked together, usually through a telescope. Wide starfield and galactic-core shots stay in plain [astrophotography](#astrophotography).

entries.name: desert_photography
entries.description: Arid country: dunes, salt flats, canyons, scrub. Marked by hard light, bare geology and long empty distances rather than by any single subject.

entries.name: garden_photography
entries.description: Cultivated grounds photographed as places: borders, paths, glasshouses, planting schemes, park views. For a single plant filling the frame use [botanical_photography](#botanical_photography).

entries.name: grand_landscape
entries.description: The sweeping vista: strong foreground, distant peaks or valley, wide lens and deep focus. The opposite of [intimate_landscape](#intimate_landscape), which crops the same country down to a patch of rock or leaves.

entries.name: industrial_landscape
entries.description: Quarries, refineries, pylons, container yards and spoil heaps read as scenery. Sits between [landscape](#landscape) and [cityscape](#cityscape); use it when infrastructure rather than a settlement fills the frame.

entries.name: intimate_landscape
entries.description: A close, edgeless piece of a [landscape](#landscape) — a stretch of riverbed, tangled branches, patterned rock — with no horizon to place it. Narrower than landscape, wider than [macro_photography](#macro_photography).

entries.name: lightning_photography
entries.description: Lightning caught with long exposures or a trigger, over land, city or sea. Usually part of [storm_photography](#storm_photography), though a single distant bolt over a calm scene counts too.

entries.name: minimalist_landscape
entries.description: A [landscape](#landscape) reduced to a few shapes against empty sky, water or snow, with large blank areas. Not simply a wide view — the emptiness is what the picture is about.

entries.name: real_estate_photography
entries.description: Rooms and exteriors shot to sell or let a property: wide lenses, tidy staging, bright even light, every space covered. Told apart from [interior_photography](#interior_photography) by purpose rather than by look.

entries.name: reef_photography
entries.description: Coral, sponges and reef fish photographed close, normally with strobes to bring the colour back. A habitat-specific slice of [underwater_photography](#underwater_photography).

entries.name: ruins_photography
entries.description: Decayed or collapsed structures photographed as they stand — ancient sites, roofless churches, burnt-out shells. Use [urban_exploration](#urban_exploration) when the point is getting inside a recently abandoned modern building.

entries.name: rural_landscape
entries.description: Farmed and grazed country: fields, hedges, barns, tracks, land shaped by work rather than left wild. Use [industrial_landscape](#industrial_landscape) where extraction or heavy plant dominates.

entries.name: safari_photography
entries.description: Animals shot from a vehicle on organised game drives: open plains, low sun, eye-level views across grass. A travel-tinged flavour of [wildlife_photography](#wildlife_photography).

entries.name: split_shot
entries.description: Half above and half below the waterline in one frame, the surface running across the middle. Shot through a dome port; the lower half means [underwater_photography](#underwater_photography) applies too.

entries.name: storm_photography
entries.description: Severe weather as the subject: supercells, shelf clouds, dust walls, blizzards, usually chased and shot from a safe distance. For the bolts themselves see [lightning_photography](#lightning_photography).

entries.name: top_down_aerial
entries.description: Camera pointed straight down, so the ground reads as a flat [pattern](#pattern) with no horizon at all. The map-like extreme of [aerial_photography](#aerial_photography).

entries.name: urban_exploration
entries.description: Abandoned or off-limits built places photographed from inside: factories, hospitals, tunnels, empty houses. Overlaps [ruins_photography](#ruins_photography), which covers weathered and ancient structures generally.

entries.name: zoo_photography
entries.description: Animals in enclosures, aquaria or sanctuaries, often framed to hide fence, glass and painted walls. Keep [wildlife_photography](#wildlife_photography) for animals that were genuinely wild.

entries.name: camera_trap
entries.description: Made by a camera left in place and fired by a motion sensor or beam, nobody behind it. Wide lens, very close animal and remote flashes are the giveaway.

entries.name: cave_photography
entries.description: Underground spaces — chambers, formations, passages — lit entirely by lamps and flashes carried in. Everything visible had to be lit by hand, which is what sets it apart from any other interior.

entries.name: photomicrography
entries.description: Made through a microscope: cells, crystals, fibres, at magnifications no camera lens reaches. Not the same as [macro_photography](#macro_photography), which uses an ordinary lens on an ordinary camera.

entries.name: planetary_photography
entries.description: Planets, the moon and the sun taken as high-frame-rate video and stacked into one sharp disc. Quite unlike [deep_sky](#deep_sky), which stacks long faint exposures instead.

entries.name: wreck_photography
entries.description: Sunken ships and aircraft photographed underwater, often in low light with a diver for scale. The submerged counterpart of [urban_exploration](#urban_exploration).

entries.name: food_photography
entries.description: Prepared food photographed to look worth eating: styled plate, chosen angle, light that shows texture and [steam](#steam). Covers both studio work and dishes shot at the table. Use [drink_photography](#drink_photography) when the subject is what is in the glass.

entries.name: product_photography
entries.description: A thing photographed so a buyer can see what it is: shape, colour, finish and scale, usually on a clean ground with even light. Use [still_life](#still_life) when the arrangement is made for its own beauty rather than for a listing.

entries.name: commercial_photography
entries.description: Any picture made to a client's brief to sell or promote something. A useful umbrella when the exact specialty is unclear. Prefer the narrower tag — [advertising_photography](#advertising_photography), [product_photography](#product_photography), [real_estate_photography](#real_estate_photography) — when you know it.

entries.name: documentary_photography
entries.description: Pictures made to record real life as it happens, over time and with a point of view, without arranging what is in front of the camera. Use [photojournalism](#photojournalism) when the work is tied to a news story and a deadline.

entries.name: flat_lay
entries.description: Objects laid out on a flat surface and shot straight down, filling the frame edge to edge. Common for food, stationery, outfits and tool kits. Use [knolling](#knolling) when everything is squared up and evenly spaced.

entries.name: photojournalism
entries.description: News photography: an event covered as it happens, staged in no way, captioned with who, where and when. Use [documentary_photography](#documentary_photography) for longer projects with no news peg, and [press_photography](#press_photography) for routine assignment coverage.

entries.name: record_shot
entries.description: A picture taken only to remember what something looked like: a serial plate, a wiring run, a parking spot, a damaged corner. Nothing is composed. Use [documentary_photography](#documentary_photography) for work made with an audience in mind.

entries.name: sports_photography
entries.description: Competition photographed as it happens: the decisive moment of play, usually a long lens, fast shutter and continuous focus from a fixed position. Use [motorsport_photography](#motorsport_photography) for racing vehicles and [press_photography](#press_photography) for the trophy handshake afterwards.

entries.name: still_life
entries.description: Inanimate things arranged and lit for their own sake: fruit, glass, cloth, tools, flowers in a vase. The arrangement is deliberate and the picture is about form, surface and light rather than sale. Use [product_photography](#product_photography) when the point is to sell the object.

entries.name: abstract_photography
entries.description: A picture where the subject is unreadable or beside the point, and shape, colour, line and texture carry it instead. Often a fragment or an extreme close-up. Use [experimental_photography](#experimental_photography) when the process itself is the departure.

entries.name: advertising_photography
entries.description: A picture built for a campaign: concept first, then styling, casting and retouching to match a layout with room for the copy. Use [product_photography](#product_photography) for a plain shot of the goods and [editorial_photography](#editorial_photography) for work made to illustrate an article.

entries.name: automotive_photography
entries.description: Cars, bikes and other vehicles photographed as objects: bodywork, panel reflections, details, often lit by a long sweep of soft light or shot at dusk. Use [motorsport_photography](#motorsport_photography) when a race is being covered.

entries.name: ecommerce_photography
entries.description: A consistent set of product pictures made for an online shop: same angles, same light, same background across every item so a grid of them looks even. Use [listing_photo](#listing_photo) for a casual private sale snapshot.

entries.name: editorial_photography
entries.description: Pictures made to run with an article in a magazine or paper — illustrating a subject rather than selling a product. Often shot loose enough to crop across a spread. Use [advertising_photography](#advertising_photography) when a brand is paying for the message.

entries.name: fine_art_photography
entries.description: Work made for its own sake and for exhibition or print sale rather than to a client's brief. Usually part of a body of work with a consistent voice. Use [commercial_photography](#commercial_photography) when someone commissioned it to sell something.

entries.name: hero_shot
entries.description: The single flattering picture of a product that leads a page or campaign, styled and lit far beyond a plain record. Reflections, spray, [steam](#steam) and props are welcome. Use [packshot](#packshot) for the plain isolated version.

entries.name: lifestyle_product_photography
entries.description: The product shown in use or in a lived-in setting rather than on a sweep: a mug on a kitchen table, boots on a trail. Hands and people may appear but the object is the subject. Use [packshot](#packshot) for the isolated version.

entries.name: listing_photo
entries.description: A quick private-sale picture for a marketplace advert: the item on a floor or table, [daylight](#daylight) from a window, flaws shown honestly. Use [ecommerce_photography](#ecommerce_photography) for a professional set shot to a house style.

entries.name: packshot
entries.description: The plain, isolated shot of a product or its packaging on white or a seamless ground, cut out or ready to be. No props, no story, nothing but the object. Use [hero_shot](#hero_shot) for the dressed-up version made to lead a campaign.

entries.name: press_photography
entries.description: Assignment coverage for publication: press conferences, court steps, ribbon cuttings, photocalls. Often a pack of photographers working from a fixed position. Use [photojournalism](#photojournalism) for reporting that follows a story rather than a diary entry.

entries.name: reference_photo
entries.description: Shot to be worked from later — by a painter, modeller, restorer or retoucher. Flat light, plain angles, several views of the same thing, no attempt at a good picture. Use [record_shot](#record_shot) when nothing will be built from it.

entries.name: staged_photography
entries.description: A scene invented and built for the camera, cast and lit like a small film set, then photographed as if found. Use [documentary_photography](#documentary_photography) for what was actually there, and [conceptual_photography](#conceptual_photography) when the staging serves a stated idea.

entries.name: stock_photography
entries.description: Generic pictures made on spec to be licensed later: clean, uncluttered, no readable brands, plenty of empty space for text. The situation is usually acted out. Use [advertising_photography](#advertising_photography) when the picture was made for one named campaign.

entries.name: tabletop_photography
entries.description: Small subjects shot on a table or bench with controlled light, usually a sweep or a cloth behind them. Describes the working method rather than the purpose, so it covers both [still_life](#still_life) and [product_photography](#product_photography) setups.

entries.name: artwork_reproduction
entries.description: A flat original — painting, drawing, print, page — copied square-on under even cross light, with colour and proportion kept true. No shadows, no perspective, no interpretation. Use [record_shot](#record_shot) for a rough documentary snapshot of the same thing.

entries.name: catalogue_photography
entries.description: Pictures made to fill a catalogue or price list, one item after another to a fixed recipe. Accuracy and repeatability matter more than drama. Use [advertising_photography](#advertising_photography) when a single picture is meant to sell an idea.

entries.name: conceptual_photography
entries.description: The picture exists to carry an idea, and everything in it was chosen to say that one thing. Often odd, deadpan or symbolic. Use [staged_photography](#staged_photography) when a scene was built but no argument is being made.

entries.name: construction_photography
entries.description: A building site recorded as it goes up, often from the same viewpoint week after week for a progress record. Cranes, formwork, muddy ground. Use [real_estate_photography](#real_estate_photography) for the finished, furnished result.

entries.name: drink_photography
entries.description: Bottles, glasses and pours photographed for the liquid: colour through the glass, condensation, bubbles, [ice](#ice). Usually [backlit](#backlit) so the drink glows. Use [food_photography](#food_photography) when a dish is the subject and the glass is only a prop.

entries.name: experimental_photography
entries.description: Work where the process is the point: chemistry abused on purpose, cameras built from tins, images made without a lens or without a camera. Use [abstract_photography](#abstract_photography) when an ordinary exposure simply has no readable subject.

entries.name: industrial_photography
entries.description: Plants, machinery, workshops and infrastructure photographed at work, usually for the company that runs them. Big spaces, mixed light, safety gear. Use [construction_photography](#construction_photography) when a site is being built rather than operated.

entries.name: inventory_photo
entries.description: One frame per item in a stocktake, collection or insurance list, usually with a label or number visible. Consistency across the set matters more than any single frame. Use [listing_photo](#listing_photo) when the thing is being sold.

entries.name: jewellery_photography
entries.description: Small reflective pieces shot with heavy diffusion and tight focus so metal reads as metal and stones keep their sparkle. Usually stacked or focus-blended for depth. Use [product_photography](#product_photography) for larger goods with ordinary surfaces.

entries.name: knolling
entries.description: A [flat_lay](#flat_lay) in which every object is aligned to right angles and spaced on an invisible grid, often sorted by size or function. The order itself is the subject. A loose scattered arrangement is just flat_lay.

entries.name: motorsport_photography
entries.description: Racing cars and bikes on a circuit or stage, usually panned so the car is sharp and everything else streaks. Use [automotive_photography](#automotive_photography) for a vehicle photographed standing still as an object.

entries.name: photo_essay
entries.description: A picture belonging to a deliberate sequence that tells one story, meant to be read in order with the others. The single frame may be quiet; the set carries the argument. Use [documentary_photography](#documentary_photography) when no sequence is intended.

entries.name: scientific_photography
entries.description: Pictures made as data: repeatable lighting, a scale reference, no retouching that changes what is shown. Covers laboratory, field and technical work. Use the narrower [photomicrography](#photomicrography) or [medical_photography](#medical_photography) when they fit.

entries.name: social_documentary
entries.description: Documentary work about how people live and what is being done to them: labour, housing, migration, poverty, protest. Made to persuade as much as to record. Use [photojournalism](#photojournalism) for coverage pegged to a single news event.

entries.name: toy_photography
entries.description: Figures, models and toys staged and lit as if they were real scenes, often at a low angle with a shallow plane of focus. The staging is the point. Use [product_photography](#product_photography) when the toy is being shown for sale.

entries.name: war_photography
entries.description: Armed conflict and its aftermath covered on the ground: fighting, damage, displacement, the people living through it. Use [social_documentary](#social_documentary) for hardship away from a war, and [photojournalism](#photojournalism) for other breaking news.

entries.name: forensic_photography
entries.description: Evidence recorded for investigation: a scene overall, then mid-range, then each item with a scale beside it. Nothing moved before the first frame. Use [record_shot](#record_shot) for ordinary documentation with no chain of custody behind it.

entries.name: medical_photography
entries.description: Clinical records of patients, procedures and pathology, shot to a fixed protocol so two dates can be compared. Neutral background, standard distance, scale in frame. Use [scientific_photography](#scientific_photography) for laboratory subjects outside the clinic.

entries.name: photogrammetry
entries.description: One frame of an overlapping set shot all round a subject so software can build measurements or a 3D model from it. Flat even light, no reflections, plenty of overlap. Individually the frames look dull and repetitive.

entries.name: specimen_photography
entries.description: A museum or laboratory object recorded against a neutral ground with a scale bar and colour reference: fossils, insects, coins, tools. Made for a collection record, not for display. Use [photomicrography](#photomicrography) when a microscope was needed.

entries.name: daylight
entries.description: Lit by the sun and the daytime sky, indoors or out, at no particular hour. The safe choice when the picture is plainly a daytime one but nothing narrower fits. Prefer [golden_hour](#golden_hour), [midday_sun](#midday_sun) or [overcast_light](#overcast_light) when you can tell.

entries.name: natural_light
entries.description: Lit by the sun, the sky or the moon, with nothing added by the photographer. Use it as the umbrella tag whenever no lamp or [flash](#flash) contributed. If a lamp was burning in the room as well, reach for [mixed_light](#mixed_light) instead.

entries.name: available_light
entries.description: Shot with whatever light was already there, nothing brought along. Overlaps [natural_light](#natural_light) but is not the same claim: available light can be a street lamp or a café bulb. Use natural_light when the source really is sun, sky or moon.

entries.name: direct_sunlight
entries.description: The sun falls straight on the subject with nothing between: bright highlights, dense shadows with crisp edges. Use it for the hard, contrasty look at any hour. If the shadows are gone and the sky is the source, that is [open_shade](#open_shade) or [overcast_light](#overcast_light).

entries.name: golden_hour
entries.description: The hour or so after [sunrise](#sunrise) and before [sunset](#sunset): warm orange light raking in from low down, long soft-edged shadows. The sun is still above the horizon and visibly lighting things. Once it has set and the warmth has gone cold, use [blue_hour](#blue_hour).

entries.name: overcast_light
entries.description: A covered sky acting as one enormous soft source: even lighting, weak shadows, muted colour. Kind to faces and to detail. Not the same as [open_shade](#open_shade), where the sky is clear and only the subject is out of the sun.

entries.name: sunset
entries.description: The sun sitting on or dropping below the horizon at the end of the day, usually with colour spread across the sky. Use it for the event itself; the warm light in the half hour before belongs to [golden_hour](#golden_hour), and what follows is [twilight](#twilight).

entries.name: window_light
entries.description: Daylight entering through a window and falling on the subject indoors, soft and strongly directional, falling off quickly across the frame. The workhorse of indoor natural-light portraits. Steady, sunless light from a north-facing opening is [north_light](#north_light).

entries.name: blue_hour
entries.description: The stretch before [sunrise](#sunrise) or after [sunset](#sunset) when the sun is below the horizon and everything is lit by a deep blue sky. City lights read as bright and warm against it. Warm raking sunlight instead means [golden_hour](#golden_hour).

entries.name: dappled_light
entries.description: Sun broken into patches by leaves or a lattice, so bright spots and shadow fall across the subject together. Pretty on a scene, difficult on a face. Even shade under the same tree, with no patches, is [deep_shade](#deep_shade).

entries.name: flat_light
entries.description: Light coming from everywhere at once, so form and depth collapse: no shadow tells you which way anything faces. Common under heavy cloud, in [fog](#fog) and on snow. Use [overcast_light](#overcast_light) when you specifically mean the cloudy sky is the source.

entries.name: long_shadows
entries.description: Shadows stretched well beyond the objects casting them, often becoming the main shape in the frame. A reliable sign of [low_sun](#low_sun) early or late in the day. Tag it when the shadows themselves are what you notice.

entries.name: low_sun
entries.description: The sun near the horizon, throwing light sideways across the scene, at either end of the day and all day in winter. Use it when the angle is the point but the colour is not especially warm; when it is warm and orange, [golden_hour](#golden_hour) is the better tag.

entries.name: midday_sun
entries.description: The sun high overhead: short shadows pooling under things, dark eye sockets on faces, bleached highlights. Use it for the awkward top-lit look of the middle of the day. If the shadows are long and raking, it is [low_sun](#low_sun).

entries.name: mixed_light
entries.description: Daylight and artificial light falling on the same scene, so one part goes blue while the other goes orange and no single white balance fixes both. Common in interiors near a window. If the lamps contribute nothing visible, tag [natural_light](#natural_light).

entries.name: moonlight
entries.description: Night lit by the moon: directional but very dim, shadows present and colour drained toward blue-grey. Usually a long exposure. A night scene lit by street lamps is not this, even if the moon is in the sky.

entries.name: open_shade
entries.description: Subject out of direct sun but under open sky, lit by the blue dome overhead: soft, even, slightly cool. The standard fallback for portraits on a sunny day. Shade with the sky blocked as well is [deep_shade](#deep_shade).

entries.name: sun_in_frame
entries.description: The sun itself is in the picture, as a disc, a blaze or a point between branches. Expect flare and a subject going toward [silhouette](#silhouette). If the sun is out of frame and only its glare washes the image, use [sun_glare](#sun_glare).

entries.name: sunrise
entries.description: The sun at or just clearing the horizon in the morning, often with the sky still cool behind it and [mist](#mist) on the ground. Tag the moment, not the whole warm period, which is [golden_hour](#golden_hour). Its evening counterpart is [sunset](#sunset).

entries.name: twilight
entries.description: The sun is below the horizon but the sky still carries light, so shapes read without being fully dark. Covers both ends of the day. The narrower, distinctly blue part of it is [blue_hour](#blue_hour); full dark under the moon is [moonlight](#moonlight).

entries.name: white_sky
entries.description: An overcast sky rendered as a blank bright patch with no detail, usually because the ground was exposed for. Tag it when that empty sky is a visible part of the frame. The lighting on the subject itself is [overcast_light](#overcast_light).

entries.name: blue_shadows
entries.description: Shadow areas rendered distinctly blue because they are lit by clear sky rather than by the sun. Most obvious on snow and white walls under sunlight. Tag it when the colour split between lit and shaded parts is the point.

entries.name: caustics
entries.description: The moving net of bright lines sunlight makes through water or glass, thrown onto a pool floor, a wall or a body. Tag it when that [pattern](#pattern) is visible in the frame. Broken tree shadow is [dappled_light](#dappled_light), not this.

entries.name: cloud_break
entries.description: A single patch of sun coming through a gap in cloud and lighting part of the scene while the rest stays dull. Tag it when the picture is built on that lit patch. Beams visible in the air instead are [god_rays](#god_rays).

entries.name: curtain_light
entries.description: Window light softened through a net or sheer curtain, so the source spreads and the shadows lose their edge. Often with the curtain itself glowing in frame. Bare window with hard sun coming in is closer to [sun_patch](#sun_patch).

entries.name: dawn_light
entries.description: The pale, cool light before the sun itself appears, when the east is brightening and shadows are barely formed. Quieter and bluer than [sunrise](#sunrise), which needs the sun in the picture or clearly on the horizon.

entries.name: deep_shade
entries.description: Shade under dense trees, an archway or a narrow street, where most of the sky is blocked too. Dim, often greenish or muddy, with little to model the subject. Shade under open sky is brighter and cleaner: use [open_shade](#open_shade).

entries.name: doorway_light
entries.description: Daylight through an open door or garage mouth, lighting the subject from one side and dying off fast into a dark interior. Bigger and lower than [window_light](#window_light), and it puts the background in near-black.

entries.name: god_rays
entries.description: Visible shafts of sunlight fanning through cloud, trees, dust or [mist](#mist). The beams themselves are the subject, not just the light they carry. Diffuse glowing air with no separate beams is [sunlight_through_fog](#sunlight_through_fog).

entries.name: hazy_sunlight
entries.description: Sun coming through [haze](#haze), thin cloud or smoke: still directional, but the shadows have soft edges and the distance goes pale. Sits between [direct_sunlight](#direct_sunlight) and [overcast_light](#overcast_light). If the air is thick enough to see beams in, use [sunlight_through_fog](#sunlight_through_fog) or [god_rays](#god_rays).

entries.name: north_light
entries.description: Light from a window or skylight that never sees the sun, so it stays soft and unchanging all day. The studio painter's light, cool and easy to work in. Any window with sun coming through it is [window_light](#window_light) or [sun_patch](#sun_patch) instead.

entries.name: reflected_sunlight
entries.description: The subject lit by sun bounced off a wall, sand, water or pavement rather than by the sun itself. Softer than [direct_sunlight](#direct_sunlight) and often tinted by whatever it bounced off. Snow doing this has its own tag, [snow_light](#snow_light).

entries.name: snow_light
entries.description: Bright light bounced up off snow, filling shadows from below and pushing everything toward white. Faces are lit from underneath and exposure runs hot. Sand and pale pavement do something similar, but tag those [reflected_sunlight](#reflected_sunlight).

entries.name: starlight
entries.description: A night frame with no moon and no lamps, lit only by the stars and airglow, so the land is barely separated from the sky. Needs a long exposure and high sensitivity. Any shadow-casting light at night points to [moonlight](#moonlight) instead.

entries.name: storm_light
entries.description: A dark, bruised sky with the sun still finding the land, so the subject is lit brightly against near-black cloud. Dramatic and short-lived, usually as weather clears. Even grey cloud with no such contrast is [overcast_light](#overcast_light).

entries.name: sun_glare
entries.description: Sunlight striking the lens from outside the frame, veiling the image with milky [haze](#haze) and washing out contrast. Usually shot into the light without a hood. When the sun disc itself is visible, tag [sun_in_frame](#sun_in_frame).

entries.name: sun_patch
entries.description: A shape of sunlight lying on a floor, wall or bed indoors, sharply bounded by the window that made it. The lit patch is the subject as much as anything in it. Light spilling in and lighting a person is [window_light](#window_light).

entries.name: sunlight_through_fog
entries.description: Sun working through [fog](#fog) or [mist](#mist), so the air itself glows and objects fade back in layers. Contrast is low and everything distant turns to [silhouette](#silhouette). Beams cutting through as distinct shafts are [god_rays](#god_rays).

entries.name: winter_light
entries.description: The thin, cool, low-angled light of the cold months, when the sun never climbs far and the day reads golden or grey all through. Use it for the seasonal character rather than a specific hour; for the angle alone, [low_sun](#low_sun) is enough.

entries.name: afterglow
entries.description: The band of colour left burning along the horizon once the sun is well down, with the rest of the sky already dark. Later and lower than [sunset](#sunset), earlier than full night. If the whole sky is evenly blue, tag [blue_hour](#blue_hour).

entries.name: alpenglow
entries.description: Pink or red light on mountains, cloud or tall buildings after the sun has left the ground, bounced down from the upper sky. The lit part is high up while everything below sits in shade. Sunlight still reaching the ground is [golden_hour](#golden_hour).

entries.name: eclipse_light
entries.description: The strange dimming of a solar eclipse: [daylight](#daylight) drained to a metallic grey, shadows still sharp, temperature dropping. Rare and unmistakable when you see it. Ordinary heavy cloud reducing the light is [overcast_light](#overcast_light).

entries.name: underwater_daylight
entries.description: Sunlight filtering down through water: everything shifts blue-green, contrast falls away with depth, and shafts may hang overhead. Tag it for pictures made under the surface with no lamp. Light patterns seen from above the water are [caustics](#caustics).

entries.name: artificial_light
entries.description: Lit by something somebody switched on or lit: a lamp, a [flash](#flash), a screen, a flame. Use it as the umbrella tag whenever the main light did not come from the sky. If [daylight](#daylight) was also falling on the subject, reach for [mixed_light](#mixed_light) instead.

entries.name: flash
entries.description: A burst of light fired with the shutter, freezing motion and usually leaving hard, fast-falling illumination. Use it for any picture that was clearly flashed, and add [on_camera_flash](#on_camera_flash) or [off_camera_flash](#off_camera_flash) when the position is obvious.

entries.name: neon_light
entries.description: Saturated tube signage or its coloured spill on faces, wet streets and walls. Strong magenta, cyan and red casts with dark surroundings. A coloured lamp aimed by the photographer is [coloured_gel](#coloured_gel) instead.

entries.name: on_camera_flash
entries.description: Flash fired straight at the subject from the camera itself: flat faces, hard-edged shadow behind, background dropping into black. The snapshot and party look. Bounce_flash uses the same unit aimed elsewhere.

entries.name: studio_lighting
entries.description: Light built from scratch on a set: stands, modifiers, a controlled background, no [daylight](#daylight) contributing. Use it for the overall look; add [softbox](#softbox), [strobe](#strobe) or [continuous_light](#continuous_light) for the actual kit when you can tell.

entries.name: bounce_flash
entries.description: Flash aimed at a ceiling or wall so the subject is lit by the rebound: softer edges, shadows under the chin, often a colour cast from the surface. Distinguish from [on_camera_flash](#on_camera_flash) by the absence of a hard wall shadow.

entries.name: candlelight
entries.description: A small, very warm flickering source close to the subject, with fast falloff into darkness and light coming from below or beside the face. Larger, more restless flame light is [firelight](#firelight).

entries.name: coloured_gel
entries.description: A coloured sheet over the light, throwing magenta, cyan or amber across the subject or the background. Usually two contrasting colours from opposite sides. Neon_light is coloured light in the scene rather than a gelled lamp.

entries.name: continuous_light
entries.description: Lamps that stay on rather than firing, so what the eye sees is what is recorded: motion blurs instead of freezing and shadows are easy to read. Covers [led_panel](#led_panel) and [tungsten_light](#tungsten_light) work. The opposite case is [flash](#flash).

entries.name: fill_flash
entries.description: A low-powered [flash](#flash) used only to open up shadows while the ambient light still carries the exposure. Backlit faces that are correctly exposed against a bright sky are the classic case. If the flash clearly dominates, use flash alone.

entries.name: flash_shadow
entries.description: A hard, sharply outlined shadow thrown onto a wall right behind the subject by a close, undiffused [flash](#flash). Use it when that shadow is a visible feature of the picture, not merely a side effect somewhere in the corner.

entries.name: fluorescent_light
entries.description: Overhead tube lighting: flat, slightly green or cyan, and unflattering on skin. Offices, shops, corridors, hospitals. If the tubes are decorative and saturated, consider [neon_light](#neon_light).

entries.name: lamplight
entries.description: Ordinary domestic lamps carrying the picture: warm pools in a room, dark corners, no [daylight](#daylight) involved. Use it for lived-in interiors at night. If the lamp itself is in shot, add [practical_light](#practical_light).

entries.name: off_camera_flash
entries.description: Flash placed away from the camera, so shadows fall to one side and the subject gains shape. Look for a shadow direction that does not match the lens axis. Studio work usually reads as [strobe](#strobe) or [studio_lighting](#studio_lighting) instead.

entries.name: practical_light
entries.description: A lamp that is visible in the frame and doing the lighting: a table lamp, a bare bulb, a strip of signage. Tag it when the source is part of the picture. If it is off-frame, use the specific source or [artificial_light](#artificial_light).

entries.name: red_eye
entries.description: Pupils glowing red because the [flash](#flash) sat close to the lens axis and lit the retina. A giveaway of [on_camera_flash](#on_camera_flash) in a dim room. Animals show it green or blue, and it still counts.

entries.name: ring_light
entries.description: A continuous ring lamp facing the subject: flat frontal light and a distinctive circular [catchlight](#catchlight) in each eye. The vlog and beauty look. A single burst with a shadow halo is [ring_flash](#ring_flash).

entries.name: screen_glow
entries.description: A face or room lit by a display: cool blue-white on one side, the rest dropping away. Phones, monitors, televisions, projectors reflected on a wall. Look for shifting colour across a face over a series.

entries.name: softbox
entries.description: A boxed, diffused light source, recognisable from its big rectangular [catchlight](#catchlight) and gentle shadow edges. Tag it when the modifier is visible or its [reflection](#reflection) gives it away. An [umbrella_light](#umbrella_light) leaves a round catchlight instead.

entries.name: speedlight
entries.description: A small portable [flash](#flash) unit, on a hotshoe or a stand, as opposed to a mains-powered studio head. Tag it when the hardware itself is visible or known. For the studio pack look, use [strobe](#strobe).

entries.name: spotlight
entries.description: One narrow beam isolating a subject against darkness, edges of the pool clearly visible. Use it for the effect in the picture, whatever made it. In a studio the equivalent hardware is [snoot](#snoot) or [grid_spot](#grid_spot).

entries.name: stage_lighting
entries.description: Concert and theatre rigs: coloured beams, deep black surroundings, extreme contrast on performers. Colour usually changes shot to shot. A single tight beam picking one figure out is [spotlight](#spotlight).

entries.name: streetlight
entries.description: Public lighting from above, throwing pools of light on pavement and hard shadows under brows. The staple of night street work. For the old amber kind specifically, use [sodium_vapour_light](#sodium_vapour_light).

entries.name: strobe
entries.description: A mains or pack powered studio [flash](#flash) head, usually behind a modifier and firing into a controlled set. Tag it for deliberate studio work; a small hotshoe unit is a [speedlight](#speedlight). The overall look is [studio_lighting](#studio_lighting).

entries.name: tungsten_light
entries.description: Warm orange light from filament bulbs or hot studio lamps, leaving skin ruddy and whites yellow unless corrected. Common in older interiors. Cool green-tinged interiors are [fluorescent_light](#fluorescent_light) instead.

entries.name: car_headlights
entries.description: Vehicle lamps lighting the scene or flaring straight into the lens, often with long streaks if the shutter was slow. Tag it when the headlights are the light source or a dominant highlight, not merely a distant dot.

entries.name: firelight
entries.description: Faces and surroundings lit by an open fire: deep orange, uneven, shadows shifting with the flame. Campfires, fireplaces, braziers. A single small flame belongs to [candlelight](#candlelight).

entries.name: flash_falloff
entries.description: The subject correctly lit while everything a few steps further back drops to black, because [flash](#flash) loses power fast with distance. Typical of night snapshots and cave or interior work. Say flash alone when the background still reads.

entries.name: led_panel
entries.description: A flat panel of LEDs used as the working light, often visible as a rectangular [catchlight](#catchlight) or standing just outside the frame. Colour is usually neutral or dialled to a chosen tint. Small on-camera panels count.

entries.name: rear_curtain_sync
entries.description: The [flash](#flash) fires at the end of a long exposure, so motion trails run behind a moving subject rather than ahead of it. Use it only when the trail direction is actually readable; otherwise [slow_sync_flash](#slow_sync_flash) is the safer tag.

entries.name: ring_flash
entries.description: A [flash](#flash) tube encircling the lens: shadowless frontal light, a thin shadow halo all round the subject, and a doughnut [catchlight](#catchlight) in the eyes. Not the same as [ring_light](#ring_light), which is continuous and shows on video and in live view.

entries.name: slow_sync_flash
entries.description: Flash combined with a long shutter, so a sharp flashed subject sits inside a smeared, ambient-lit background. Nightclub and street-at-night pictures with trailing highlights. Rear_curtain_sync is the variant where the trail runs behind the subject.

entries.name: string_lights
entries.description: Chains of small bulbs strung through a scene, usually warm and usually out of focus behind the subject. A common source of round background highlights at parties and markets.

entries.name: umbrella_light
entries.description: Flash or lamp fired into or through a photographic umbrella: broad, spilling light and a round [catchlight](#catchlight) with visible ribs. Less controlled than a [softbox](#softbox), which contains its spill.

entries.name: beauty_dish
entries.description: A shallow metal dish giving crisp but not harsh light, a defined shadow under the nose and a bright ring [catchlight](#catchlight). Used close and slightly above the face in [portrait](#portrait) work. Softer, larger results belong to [softbox](#softbox).

entries.name: blacklight
entries.description: Ultraviolet lamps making whites, teeth and paint fluoresce against a near-black room, with a violet cast over everything. Club and party work. Not the same as [coloured_gel](#coloured_gel), which tints ordinary light.

entries.name: flicker_banding
entries.description: Horizontal bands of brightness or colour across the frame, caused by a fast shutter or rolling shutter reading a mains-flickering lamp. Common indoors and under LED signage. Not a processing fault, so do not tag it as noise.

entries.name: gobo
entries.description: A cut-out or cutter placed in front of a lamp to throw a shaped shadow: window bars, leaves, blinds, a slatted [pattern](#pattern) across a wall. Tag it when the pattern was clearly made, not cast by a real window.

entries.name: grid_spot
entries.description: A honeycomb grid over the light, restricting the beam so it lands where it is aimed and the background stays dark. Look for a soft-edged pool rather than the hard circle of a [snoot](#snoot).

entries.name: high_speed_sync
entries.description: Flash used above the camera's normal sync speed so a wide aperture can be held in bright sun. Shows as a flashed subject with a dark, controlled sky and shallow focus at midday. A specialist tag; only use it when the setup is known.

entries.name: laser_light
entries.description: Thin, hard-edged coloured beams cutting through a room, often visible only because of [haze](#haze) or smoke. Concerts, clubs and installations. Broader coloured beams from a rig are [stage_lighting](#stage_lighting).

entries.name: snoot
entries.description: A tube on the light that narrows it to a small circular pool, leaving the rest of the frame dark. Use it for a tight, hard-edged patch of light on a face or an object. A [grid_spot](#grid_spot) does the same job with a softer edge.

entries.name: sodium_vapour_light
entries.description: The heavy orange monochrome glow of old sodium street lamps, which flattens every colour it touches towards amber. Mostly older night city work. Newer white or blue-white street lighting is just [streetlight](#streetlight).

entries.name: stroboscopic_flash
entries.description: Repeated flashes during one exposure, printing a moving subject several times across the frame. Look for evenly spaced ghost copies of one figure. A single [flash](#flash) with a motion trail is [slow_sync_flash](#slow_sync_flash) instead.

entries.name: backlit
entries.description: The main light sits behind the subject, so the front is in shadow and the edges glow. Use it whenever the light source faces the camera, whether or not it is in frame. For a subject reduced to a black shape use [silhouette](#silhouette) instead.

entries.name: hard_light
entries.description: A small or distant source gives shadows with sharp, clearly drawn edges and an abrupt jump from lit to unlit. Bare bulbs and clear sun do it. Judge by the shadow edge, not by brightness; a blurred edge means [soft_light](#soft_light).

entries.name: side_lighting
entries.description: Light arrives from roughly ninety degrees to the camera, lighting one side of the subject and leaving the other in shadow. It is the classic texture-revealing direction. When the two sides are hard-edged and equal, use [split_lighting](#split_lighting).

entries.name: soft_light
entries.description: A large source relative to the subject gives shadows that fade out gradually with no defined edge, and gentle modelling on faces. The opposite of [hard_light](#hard_light). Light softened by passing through something is [diffused_light](#diffused_light).

entries.name: cast_shadow
entries.description: A shadow thrown by something onto another surface is a visible element of the picture, not just an absence of light. Railings, blinds and plants do it. When the shape is a deliberate stencil or [gobo](#gobo), use [patterned_light](#patterned_light).

entries.name: catchlight
entries.description: The [reflection](#reflection) of the light source in the subject's eye, showing the source shape and roughly where it stood. Worth tagging when it is prominent or unusual, such as a ring or a double catchlight from [clamshell_lighting](#clamshell_lighting).

entries.name: diffused_light
entries.description: The source has been spread by a scrim, [softbox](#softbox), curtain or cloud before reaching the subject, so it arrives soft and from a wide area. Use it when the softening is visible in the picture; [soft_light](#soft_light) is the broader tag for the result alone.

entries.name: directional_light
entries.description: The light clearly comes from one identifiable direction, so the subject has a lit side and a shadow side and the form is modelled. Says nothing about hardness. When no direction can be read, use [even_lighting](#even_lighting).

entries.name: even_lighting
entries.description: Light of roughly equal strength across the whole frame, with no dominant direction and barely any shadow. Typical of copy work, product tables and heavy cloud. If a direction is readable, use [directional_light](#directional_light) instead.

entries.name: fill_light
entries.description: A secondary, weaker light or reflector that lifts the shadow side without creating shadows of its own. Visible as detail in the dark half rather than as a source. Unfilled shadows that go black instead push the picture toward [high_contrast_lighting](#high_contrast_lighting).

entries.name: front_lighting
entries.description: The light comes from behind the camera and falls straight onto the subject, so shadows fall away out of sight. Colours read cleanly but form goes flat. If there is no modelling at all across the frame, [even_lighting](#even_lighting) fits better.

entries.name: high_contrast_lighting
entries.description: A wide gap between the lit and shadowed parts, with highlights near white and shadows near black and little in between. Comes from an unfilled hard source. The heavily dark, dramatic version of it is [chiaroscuro](#chiaroscuro).

entries.name: key_light
entries.description: The dominant source that decides where the shadows fall; tag it when the picture is clearly built around one identifiable main light. The weaker source that opens those shadows is [fill_light](#fill_light). Which side it comes from is a separate tag.

entries.name: rim_light
entries.description: A bright line traces the edge of the subject, separating it from the background. It comes from behind and to one side. Use [hair_light](#hair_light) when the line sits only on the top of the head, and [kicker_light](#kicker_light) when it rakes a cheek or shoulder from behind.

entries.name: specular_highlight
entries.description: A mirror-like bright spot where the source reflects off a glossy surface: skin, metal, glass, wet ground. Its size and shape tell you how big the light was. A highlight seen specifically in an eye is a [catchlight](#catchlight).

entries.name: top_lighting
entries.description: The source is directly above the subject, dropping shadows into the eye sockets and under the nose and chin. Common under ceiling fixtures and at midday. Light from above and slightly in front that leaves a small nose shadow is [butterfly_lighting](#butterfly_lighting).

entries.name: backlit_translucency
entries.description: Light passing through a thin subject makes it glow from within: leaves, petals, fabric, ears, liquid in a glass. Distinct from [rim_light](#rim_light), which only draws the outline while the body stays dark.

entries.name: bounced_light
entries.description: The light reaches the subject after reflecting off a wall, ceiling, card or nearby surface, arriving soft and often coloured by whatever it hit. Look for a shadow direction that does not match any visible lamp.

entries.name: chiaroscuro
entries.description: Most of the frame is dark, with a single directional source picking out a small lit area, in the painterly manner. Stronger and more deliberate than plain [high_contrast_lighting](#high_contrast_lighting), and it usually needs unfilled shadows and a visible falloff into black.

entries.name: contre-jour
entries.description: Shooting straight into the light so the subject is rendered dark against a bright field, often with flare or [haze](#haze). It is the extreme case of [backlit](#backlit), where the source is nearly on the lens axis. If the shape reads as pure black, tag [silhouette](#silhouette) too.

entries.name: hair_light
entries.description: A small light from above and behind that puts a sheen on the top of the head and lifts hair off the background. Portrait-specific. A bright line running down the whole body outline is [rim_light](#rim_light) instead.

entries.name: kicker_light
entries.description: A light placed low and well behind the subject that grazes one side, adding a hot streak along a cheek, jaw or shoulder. Narrower and more angled than [rim_light](#rim_light), and it does not necessarily wrap the whole outline.

entries.name: low_contrast_lighting
entries.description: Highlights and shadows sit close together, giving a soft, grey, gentle rendering of the subject. Comes from wide, well-filled or diffused sources. Do not use it for a low-contrast look created in processing rather than by the light.

entries.name: patterned_light
entries.description: The source is broken up by a cutter, stencil or slatted object so the light lands as a repeated shape on the subject. Distinguish from [cast_shadow](#cast_shadow), where the shadow is incidental rather than shaped on purpose.

entries.name: raking_light
entries.description: Light skimming across a surface at a very shallow angle, so every ridge, brushstroke or fold throws its own long shadow. Used to read texture in walls, paper and paintings. Reserve it for surfaces; a person lit from the side is [side_lighting](#side_lighting).

entries.name: three_quarter_lighting
entries.description: The light sits about forty-five degrees off the camera axis, between [front_lighting](#front_lighting) and [side_lighting](#side_lighting), so most of the face is lit and one cheek carries shadow. The workhorse [portrait](#portrait) angle. Its named variants are [loop_lighting](#loop_lighting) and [rembrandt_lighting](#rembrandt_lighting).

entries.name: underlighting
entries.description: The light comes from below the subject, throwing shadows upward and inverting the shading a face normally has. Screens, campfires and footlights do it. It reads as unsettling or theatrical, which is usually the point of tagging it.

entries.name: broad_lighting
entries.description: The side of the face turned toward the camera is the lit one, widening the visible features while the far side falls into shadow. The mirror of [short_lighting](#short_lighting); check which cheek carries the light before choosing.

entries.name: rapid_falloff
entries.description: Brightness drops away steeply within the frame, so a subject close to the source is bright while the background a step behind goes black. A sign of a small source placed close. The opposite reads as [even_lighting](#even_lighting).

entries.name: short_lighting
entries.description: The side of the face turned away from the camera is the lit one, so the near cheek stays in shadow. It narrows the face. The opposite arrangement is [broad_lighting](#broad_lighting).

entries.name: wraparound_light
entries.description: A very large or heavily bounced source curls around the subject, so even the far side keeps detail and the shadow line is hard to place. Softer still than ordinary [soft_light](#soft_light), and typical of a big window close by.

entries.name: black_background
entries.description: The subject is lit and the background records as pure black, either by unlit distance from the backdrop or by flagging the light off it. Differs from [low_key](#low_key), which describes the whole tonal scheme rather than just the backdrop.

entries.name: high_key
entries.description: Bright, low-contrast lighting where almost everything sits in the upper tones, usually against a white background lit as bright as the subject. Shadows are present but very open. Not the same as an [overexposed](#overexposed) frame — highlights still hold detail.

entries.name: low_key
entries.description: Dark, high-contrast lighting where most of the frame falls away to black and a small lit area carries the picture. Usually one tightly controlled source with heavy [negative_fill](#negative_fill). A dim snapshot is not low_key; the darkness has to be deliberate.

entries.name: seamless_backdrop
entries.description: A roll of paper or cloth curving from wall to floor with no visible join, so the subject stands in an empty field of one tone. Tag the seamless itself; add [white_background](#white_background) or [black_background](#black_background) for the tone it was lit to.

entries.name: softbox_lighting
entries.description: Key fired through a fabric box, giving soft-edged shadows and a rectangular [catchlight](#catchlight) in the eyes. The most common studio look of all. The catchlight shape is what separates it from [umbrella_lighting](#umbrella_lighting).

entries.name: white_background
entries.description: The subject stands against a background lit to clean white with no visible texture or shadow, as in catalogue and cut-out work. Tag it whether the white came from lighting the backdrop or from a light tent.

entries.name: butterfly_lighting
entries.description: Key placed high and directly in front, throwing a small butterfly-shaped shadow straight down under the nose. Flatters cheekbones and is common in beauty work. Add a light from below and it becomes [clamshell_lighting](#clamshell_lighting).

entries.name: clamshell_lighting
entries.description: A soft source above the face and a reflector or second source directly below, closing on the subject like a shell. Gives almost shadowless skin and a double [catchlight](#catchlight) in each eye. Without the lower source it is [butterfly_lighting](#butterfly_lighting).

entries.name: loop_lighting
entries.description: Key slightly above eye level and around thirty to forty-five degrees off axis, leaving a small nose shadow angled down the cheek but not touching it. The everyday [portrait](#portrait) [pattern](#pattern). Once that shadow joins the cheek shadow it is [rembrandt_lighting](#rembrandt_lighting).

entries.name: one_light_setup
entries.description: A single source doing all the work, with shadows left to fall where they will or opened up by a reflector. Look for one consistent shadow direction and no separation light on the hair. Add the [pattern](#pattern) tag it makes, such as [rembrandt_lighting](#rembrandt_lighting).

entries.name: reflector_fill
entries.description: A white, silver or gold panel bouncing the key back into the shadows instead of a second lamp. Gives a soft lift with no extra shadow, and often a broad low [catchlight](#catchlight). If a real lamp is doing it, use [fill_light](#fill_light).

entries.name: rembrandt_lighting
entries.description: Key high and about forty-five degrees off to one side, leaving a small triangle of light on the shadow cheek under the eye. The triangle closing the loop under the nose is the test. If the shadow stays a detached blob beside the nose it is [loop_lighting](#loop_lighting).

entries.name: split_lighting
entries.description: Key at ninety degrees to the face so one half is lit and the other falls into shadow, split down the nose. Dramatic and unforgiving of skin texture. With a little wrap and a triangle on the far cheek it is [rembrandt_lighting](#rembrandt_lighting) instead.

entries.name: strobe_lighting
entries.description: Flash heads as the working light: frozen motion, clean shadow edges and no ambient colour cast. Look for crisp detail even where the room was dim. Lamps left burning through the exposure are [continuous_lighting](#continuous_lighting).

entries.name: three_point_lighting
entries.description: The standard arrangement of a key on one side, a softer fill on the other, and a light behind separating the subject from the background. Recognisable by a shaped face plus a bright edge on hair or shoulders. Use [one_light_setup](#one_light_setup) when only the key is working.

entries.name: umbrella_lighting
